regressions.found: 2026-09-24, review of this task's DI-9 wiring
regressions.defect: DI-9 matched the policy's question_required patterns with path.starts_with(pattern) in crates/verification, not with ProtectedSurface::matches grammar: no segment pattern (/deploy/, /deployment/, /release/, /infra/, /terraform/, /k8s/, /helm/) matched a relative path, .tf matched no Terraform file, Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml/Jenkinsfile matched only at the root; deploy/prod.yaml and infra/main.tf were written without a typed question.
regressions.audit: BROKEN-DRIFTED: wired to the policy, matched by a second matcher; first missing link the DI-9 predicate in evaluate_file.
regressions.fix: ProtectedSurface::matches delegates to ProtectedSurface::matches_patterns (crates/policy, grammar unchanged); DI-9 calls it. No new dependency edge; the fallback .github/ and .modbit/ decide as before; risk rules and policy version unchanged.
regressions.negative_proof: Run before the fix: four of the five unit tests fail (deploy/prod.yaml, infra/main.tf, services/api/Dockerfile) and the Core test finds no DiffInvariantViolated for services/api/deploy/prod.yaml; the root-prefix/fallback test passes before and after.
regressions.limitations: DI-9 stays a permanent DENY: no answered typed question lifts it (UserQuestionAnswered feeds only the docs/28 §3 scope unlock); follow-up, not part of this regression.

regressions.found: 2026-09-24, EPR-019 held-out risk corpus (benchmarks/gate-calibration/corpora/risk-holdout.json, case env-production)
regressions.defect: derive_realized_risk classified a change to config/.env.production as LOW with no review and no human: the secret surface's `.env` pattern matched only as a path suffix, so every .env.<name> file (the credential files docs/23's protected paths deny as **/.env.*) fell through; the surface also lacked the other credential stores docs/23 protects (.ssh/, id_rsa*, id_ed25519*, .netrc, .npmrc, .pypirc), and suffixes were case-sensitive, so certs\Server.KEY was not a secret.
regressions.audit: BROKEN-DRIFTED: the rule set had drifted from docs/23's protected paths; first missing link: no pattern shape for a basename prefix.
regressions.fix: REALIZED_RISK_RULES_VERSION risk-rules-2: a basename-prefix pattern shape (.env.*) carried by the secret surface with the other docs/23 credential stores (/.ssh/ segment, id_rsa*, id_ed25519*, .netrc, .npmrc, .pypirc); a suffix or basename prefix is compared without ASCII case; directories, segments and basenames stay exact; a suffix has no '/', so only a basename's end matches (environment.rs, dotenv.rs, hotkey.rs match nothing). Default policy version assurance-8531202d7bf6dd6d -> assurance-2b11ce09853c8650. A Core drift guard requires every DEFAULT_PROTECTED credential glob to be on the secret surface. DI-9 uses the same matcher (d036dd1), so question-required suffixes are case-insensitive too (a strengthening). EPR-008 corpus re-pinned 23 -> 29 cases (existing diagnoses move only their two versions).
regressions.negative_proof: Disposable mutations, restored: without the .env.* pattern the unit test fails on config/.env.production, the corpus pin fails, and the real-Core test fails because the unattended local_autonomous run rewriting config/.env.production reaches ReadyForReview (the defect reproduced through production routing); with case-sensitive suffixes the unit test fails on certs\Server.KEY and the pin on secret_extension_upper_case; without the six store patterns the drift guard fails on .ssh/x (protected by .ssh/**), the store unit test and the pin fail.
regressions.limitations: Not covered, as docs/23 does not protect them either: Windows curl's _netrc and id_ecdsa*/id_dsa* keys.

regressions.found: 2026-09-25, the limitation recorded by the di-9-matcher regression: DI-9 was a permanent DENY
regressions.defect: docs/64 §4 says a protected path changes only after a typed question, but evaluate_file raised DI-9 whenever the path matched the policy, invariant_context filled the paths without reference to any answer, and UserQuestionAnswered fed only the scope unlock of docs/28 §3: after the user said yes to changing deploy/prod.yaml the write was still refused DIFF_INVARIANT_DENY.
regressions.audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL: the DENY half was wired, the typed-question half did not exist; first missing link nothing carried an answered question into InvariantContext.
regressions.fix: user.ask takes `paths`; handle_ask records the DI-9-protected ones on UserQuestionAsked.protected_paths and sets Core-owned continue/stop options labelled with them; only an Actor::User `continue` unlocks, recorded as ProtectedPathsUnlocked by Actor::Core("change-engine") and rebuilt only from the Core into InvariantContext.protected_unlocked (exact paths); headless and no_approval_profiles tasks fail closed PROTECTED_PATH_FAIL_CLOSED.
regressions.negative_proof: Run before the fix on the pre-fix Core (8d1f742): the user's yes to a question naming deploy/prod.yaml left the next write DI-9 DENY; the positive, declined and fail-closed tests fail; five runtime mutations (unlock not reaching InvariantContext, any actor, any option, no fail-closed refusal, the model's options standing) each turn exactly their test red.
regressions.limitations: The unlock belongs to one task and names exact paths (a fork must ask again; no directory unlock). A question naming protected paths asked while a scope expansion waits also counts as the scope question (docs/28 §3); narrowing that to questions naming the waiting paths is an open follow-up.
